flows.name: 1. Single pass from the window (Calibrate -> Prescan/Scan -> meter -> USB bytes -> decode/direction -> shading -> library.save -> compact -> corrected view / Save As)

steps.does: A measurement starts only after the 'The film is in the transport' tick (choose() at ~2117 refuses otherwise); 'reuse' with an existing cache (_cached_reference 1984) skips the question. Submits Calibrate(mode, reference=session.reference) and sets self.calibrated=True optimistically; the 'calibrated' event later overwrites it.

skip -> no reference; reuse and file exists -> load_shading (713, origin {'action':'loaded', path, file mtime, loaded_utc}, no archive link); otherwise calibrate_shading(keep_data=True). _calibrate sets session.calibrated from summary action and reference; only an exception keeps the earlier in-memory reference -- a calibration that returns None overwrites DirectScanner._shading with None (direct.py:2351).
steps.data: Path of the cache; summary dict

steps.does: _refuse_if_suspect; _CommandLog.start; READ STATE x<=4, wait_warm, TUR; exposure+highlight WRITEs; calibration-info WRITE+READ(128); SET FRAME (0,3431,10343,6888); cmd 0x17; gain/offset read-back+write; MODE SELECT (3600 dpi, one-pass colour, 8-bit, INDEX, calibrate); SLIDE INIT param 0x01; wait_ready; shading descriptor (width from descriptor, fallback frame); START SCAN; 10 s silence; TUR; loop {set_gain_offset(get_gain_offset()); read_lines(4, 2*width+2, retries=1)} until EndOfData OR any ScanReadError (a refused read is treated as the normal end, ended=True, no minimum line count checked); deadline 300 s -> suspect + raise; get_ccd_mask(width); finish_scan; calculate_shading (shading.py:109) splits dark/light lines per channel by the widest level-ratio gap, single-point fallback when max/min < 5
steps.data: raw calibration bytes (16-bit tagged lines, ~1.66 MB) -> ShadingReference{ref/dark: float64[width] per channel 0-2, mean/dark_mean floats, pixels_per_line} + width-byte CCD mask + command log dict {sent:[{t,cdb,out,in|refused}], image_reads}
steps.persists: in memory: _shading, _ccd_mask (only when shading not None), _shading_origin {'action':'calibrated', resolution, width, measured_utc} (set even when no reference resulted)

steps.does: calibration/<UTC>[-N]/data.bin (exact bytes, plain write), ccd_mask.bin, shading.npz (np.savez_compressed via ShadingReference.save), calibration.json (width, stride, resolution, commands, sha256, protocol_revision) while the device is open; archive path added to _shading_origin; cache written to .shading.part.npz then os.replace (no retry). OSError on either is logged and swallowed.
window sets self.calibrated from event.done and relabels the button

Prescan(resolution 25-7200, film): scan(depth 8, RGB, FULL_FRAME, shading=True, keep_raw=True, film); meta = scanner.last_scan_meta; raw_image = last_pixels_raw; _last_prescan=(corrected image, position, meta) kept for reversal judging; _deliver; _file(kind='prescan', number 0, tags gui/prescan) -> writer (compress=False), out_dir copy under out_dir/prescans/

asks to calibrate if not; _dpi() 25-7200 (no correctable_at check here; scan() refuses >3600); _exposure() only parses numbers (0 or negative accepted, later clamped to 100 by Settings.scaled); _pin_arrangement copies current.rotation/flipped into session.rotation/flip from the UI thread; submits Scan(...) with shading default True, frame None
steps.data: Scan(resolution, infrared, fast_infrared, film, auto_exposure, exposure_scale, mono, mono_channel, notes, tags) (session.py:1384)

steps.does: Refusals before any command: infrared on B&W/Kodachrome (ValueError ~2895); shading and not correctable_at (uncorrectable ~2947); no/too-narrow reference (uncalibrated ~2963). No _refuse_if_suspect at the top: a suspect device is refused only at SLIDE INIT / START SCAN.

base=get_gain_offset; up to rounds(+1 if clipped) probes: set_gain_offset(base) then self.scan(300 dpi, RGB, 16-bit, exposure_scale=scales, shading, keep_raw=True) -- film NOT passed, so each probe's meta says film='negative'; each probe has its own command log and debug spool item; metering_slice from round 1; 99.5th percentile/65535; asymmetric tolerance; growth clamped to 65535/base exposure; last_metering dict (scales/levels/targets rounded 4 dp). Returned scales are full precision.
steps.persists: probes only through the debug spool (RPS7200_DEBUG)

steps.does: _CommandLog.start (direct.py:455); READ STATE x<=4, wait_warm, TUR, READ STATE (media bit logged only); WRITE exposure/highlight; SET FRAME; cmd 0x17; READ GAIN/OFFSET -> Settings.scaled (protocol.py:601, int, clamp 100..65535) -> WRITE GAIN/OFFSET; MODE SELECT (INDEX, byte14_for or override, fast-IR bit gated on infrared); TUR; SLIDE INIT param 0x16 (refuses if suspect); wait_ready; carriage_record
steps.data: Settings ints; command log entries (cdb/out/in hex, refused name)

steps.where: rps7200/direct.py:3237 _read_pass -> 1605 start_scan, 1735 get_ccd_mask, 1746 get_parameters, 1799 read_planes -> 1757 read_lines -> rps7200/usb_transport.py:772 command -> 717 _read_payload
steps.does: Batch READs; NoDataYet re-polled every 20 ms up to read_idle_s (120 s; 287 s untied IR), each poll logged as a 'refused' command entry; _read_payload returns exactly read_size bytes or raises (NoDataYet if nothing, UsbError on mid-payload stall); a payload followed by CHECK is dropped as CheckCondition; EndOfData before total_lines breaks the loop and the short pass is accepted with _read_complete=True (no suspect, no error). Chunks joined; last_raw/last_raw_layout kept when keep_raw or debug, else cleared; decode_index (1923) splits by tag into <u2/u1 planes, truncates to the common height, read_direction (direction.py:85) from tags, reverses rows if bottom-up; finish_scan; any exception before the last line marks suspect.
steps.data: bytes channels*lines*(bpl+2) -> ndarray (H,W,C) uint16|uint8 upright; mask bytes sized to the reference width; ScanParameters

steps.does: 7200 dpi stagger realignment (trims NATIVE_COLUMN_STAGGER_LINES=4 rows, recorded as stagger_realigned); raw_pixels kept; apply_shading (shading.py:196) two-point per column through the mask, depth-scaled, clamped, columns beyond the mask's used count left raw; meta dict (protocol_revision, shading report, shading_skipped, exposure/gain/offset, exposure_scale, exposure_metered=bool(auto_exposure), fast_infrared, filter_offsets, read_direction, stagger_realigned, started_utc, mode, commands, shading_origin, carriage_state; metering only when this scan metered); _debug_capture(raw_pixels, meta) spools when debug; last_pixels_raw/last_scan_meta set; returns the corrected copy
raw_image = last_pixels_raw; reversal judged against the last prescan only for passes whose direction is unknown (adds meta['reversal']); a <=1400 px contiguous copy goes to the UI as a Result event

out_dir name picked now with _unclaimed; capture_record (direct.py:889: reference, ccd_mask, raw bytes, layout of the LAST pass); raw_bytes_disagree (session.py:734) drops bytes of another shape; reversal composed with _orientation_for into meta rotation/flipped; raw_image of another shape dropped (corrected pixels then filed, labelled); debug_claim(raw_image); FrameWriter.submit(compress=bool(roll) -> False here, paths=[out_dir copy])
steps.data: job dict with corrected image, raw_image, meta, capture
steps.thread: scanner worker (blocks when the writer queue of 2 is full)

steps.does: preview.orient + to_monochrome for delivery only; library.save: _reserve dir, INCOMPLETE marker, scan.tif (raw decode, uncompressed), prescan.tif if any, shading.npz (savez_compressed), ccd_mask.bin, raw.bin (plain, streamed sha256), scan.json via _write_atomic (fsync + single os.replace), marker removed, reindex (non-atomic index.json); corrections=['shading'] only when raw_image is None and meta.shading set; then export.write of each path (in place); a library failure raises before any copy is attempted (F01); on_done -> ScanSession._filed -> 'filed' event
steps.data: raw uint16/uint8 pixels, bytes, float64 reference, JSON record

steps.does: hides a superseded prescan at the same transport position, composes reversal with the photograph's orientation, shows the working copy; 'filed' sets result.entry by seq
reads scan.tif + shading.npz + ccd_mask.bin and applies today's apply_shading (or returns raw with a reason); handed back through self._reads queue

library.corrected(entry) -> preview.orient(result.rotation, result.flipped) -> to_monochrome if the WINDOW's current v_mono is ticked (not the pass's film) -> export.write(path) with no resolution tag; falls back to the reduced working copy when not filed yet
steps.thread: UI (Save As) / save-all or export-rolls daemon

steps.where: rps7200/session.py:1966-1994 (_run finally) -> rps7200/direct.py:1134 close -> 1031 _debug_flush; rps7200/library.py:414 compact
steps.does: scanner.close() unless force-aborted (dead): transport closed, then unclaimed spooled passes filed with library.save(compress=True) into $RPS7200_DEBUG_ROOT or ./library (claimed ones only unlinked); if t.close() raises the flush is skipped; writer.finish; unsaved manifests re-saved; library.compact for every entry in writer.uncompressed (raw.bin -> raw.bin.gz verified by sha256, TIFFs rewritten compressed via _replace_tiff, record updated, raw.bin unlinked)
steps.thread: scanner worker (after the writer has finished)
steps.persists: library/<id>/raw.bin.gz, recompressed TIFFs, updated scan.json; debug entries

steps.does: argparse and pre-open refusals: IR on B&W/Kodachrome, bracket 2-9, dpi>0, correctable_at unless --no-shading, --out extension, stops>0, --bracket with --ir, bracket exposure-scale arity; fast_ir cleared without --ir; say_estimate

DeferredInterrupt installed (first Ctrl-C only sets a flag, checked only between bracket passes); DirectScanner(debug=None) opened; inquiry; ensure_shading(ref_path, reuse, skip=--no-shading) with no question about film; reuse loads calibration/shading.npz when present, otherwise Flow 1 steps 2-3

s.scan(resolution, infrared, exposure_scale, auto_exposure, film, shading, keep_raw=library is not None, fast_infrared) (Flow 1 steps 8-12); hold() appends raw pixels (last_pixels_raw), meta, capture (reference, mask, raw bytes, layout) and inquiry to `pending` in RAM and claims the pass

scales from --exposure-scale / auto_exposure (last_metering not attached to any pass) / 1.0; geometric ladder topped at the 16-bit timer ceiling; each pass scan(exposure_scale=scale*k) with meta bracket_index/ratio/passes/stops; on_pass keeps sensor pixels (raw, or a rail map without the library) and calls hold(); corrected frames retained; hold raises _StoppedBetweenPasses after Ctrl-C

after the context exits (close -> debug flush of unclaimed metering probes on the main thread) each pending pass is filed with library.save(compress=True): raw.bin.gz, deflate TIFF, shading.npz, ccd_mask.bin, scan.json; not wrapped in try

bracket: merge_bracket(corrected frames, ratios, sensor_frames|sensor_rails) and meta['bracket']; mono default for --film bw; export.write(--out, resolution=dpi) + <out>.json (meta incl. commands). The merged image exists only in --out
--reuse: load_shading sets _shading_origin {'action':'loaded', path, file_modified_utc, loaded_utc} (no archive link) and every corrected pass records it in extra.shading_origin

flows.name: 3. Roll: walk -> frame edges -> contact sheet -> approved.json -> Roll -> holds/nudges -> per-frame scan -> FrameWriter -> library + frameNN.tif + roll.json

steps.does: validates range and dpi 25-7200 (window: no correctable_at; CLI refuses it for non-dry runs at 332), warns when frame_edges cannot read that prescan dpi/film, chooses the folder (roll_dir), clears or keeps the sheet, EdgeWatch.begin; submits Roll(dry_run, out=folder, prescan_resolution, correct, ...). CLI: seek then calibrate(), survey.json replaced (.bak) or roll.json carried forward

seek (wait_warm, _ask_position, checked rewind/advance, verify arrival else FilmNotPlaced) before anything is written; folder mkdir; survey.json (walk) or roll.json (roll); earlier manifest carried (live RollManifest, or earlier_manifest + keep_first_numbering + renumbered); settings block; RollManifest; _frame_rotation/_frame_flip from approved

checks meter/film/IR (not resolution); baseline=get_gain_offset; StripWalk when correcting; per index: place_on_strip, skip unchosen, prescan(prescan_resolution, 8-bit, corrected, film) -> raw_prescan/prescan_meta; frame_contrast below blank ends the roll (that prescan is yielded to nobody and filed only by debug); registration marks; walk.observe; approved -> _hold_to_approved; correct -> _aim_frame; the verification prescan replaces prescan/raw_prescan/prescan_meta; dry run yields RollFrame(prescan, raw_prescan, prescan_meta, marks, prescan_before); caught failures yield RollFrame(error, prescan, raw_prescan, prescan_meta); suspect ends the roll

measure_shift_mm(reference, prescan) -> hold_plan -> nudge (param_for_mm clamp 1..87; SLIDE 00|01 param 00 04) -> sleep HOLD_SETTLE_S 0.4 -> verification prescan(prescan_resolution, keep_raw, shading) WITHOUT film (meta film='negative') -> repeat; first-move wrong-way check sets roll_abort; marks['approved'|'correction'] = history/confidence/final_mm/residual_mm/row_reversed
steps.persists: verification prescans only through the debug spool

steps.does: METER_EACH/ONCE: set_gain_offset(baseline), auto_exposure -> scales; set_gain_offset(baseline); scan(resolution, IR, window, exposure_scale=scales, keep_raw) recorded exposure_metered False with no metering record; meta roll_index, roll_position, registration=marks; yield RollFrame(image corrected, raw_image, prescan corrected, raw_prescan, prescan_meta)

_deliver prescan; only when job.dry_run: _file(corrected prescan, dict(prescan_meta, roll_membership), raw_image=raw_prescan, path=rolls/<roll>/prescanNN.tif) -> FrameWriter (compress=True) -> library entry of the raw prescan with its own mask/bytes + prescanNN.tif (corrected, oriented by the session pair); prescan_before -> prescanNN-before.tif only (file_entry=False); RollManifest.record -> survey.json (registration, prescan file, prescan_rotation/flipped)

tiff.write(prescanNN.tif) and prescanNN-before.tif (deflate, unoriented) on the scanning thread with the device open; FrameWriter entry of the raw prescan with capture guarded by raw_bytes_disagree and debug_claim
each walked prescan working copy is read for frame edges against the other frames; offsets and notes (measured/unconfirmed/neighbours/none) published by version

sheet from survey results (corrected prescans), proposals, ticks, offsets (snapped), per-frame rotation/flip; state kept via _store_sheet_state (2666) in gui-settings.json 'sheet'[key]; reopen re-reads prescanNN.tif (un-oriented by prescan_arrangement), survey.json, roll.json, approved.json

validates sheet dpi 25-7200 (no correctable_at), pins predpi to the survey's, builds Approved(number, offset_mm snapped, rotation, flipped, reference=working-copy prescan array, reference_entry, source), confirms, merges rolls/<roll>/approved.json (offset_mm rounded 4 dp, write_manifest with .bak), submits Roll(only, approved, start_at, frames=span, out=folder, mono). CLI equivalent tools/scan_roll.py:230-307 hold_from_walk -> walked_prescans + preview.unorient(tiff.read(prescanNN.tif)) -> frame_edges.propose_centred

rf.error: logged only -- that frame's prescan and raw prescan are not filed (real roll). Otherwise _note_reversal vs the frame's prescan; _deliver; _file(image, meta+roll_membership, raw_image, prescan=rf.prescan (corrected; raw_prescan dropped), prescan_meta, path=frameNN.tif (not _unclaimed), mono, on_filed); FrameWriter gzips while the next frame scans: library.save (raw scan.tif, raw.bin.gz, shading.npz, ccd_mask.bin, prescan.tif corrected, scan.json) then export frameNN.tif (corrected, oriented, mono) + out_dir copy; a filing error makes _filed request_stop

writer.submit(image, raw_image, prescan=frame.prescan, capture=s.capture_record()) with no mono, rotate or flip keys and no raw_bytes_disagree guard; FrameWriter has no on_done, so filing failures do not stop the roll; error frames' prescans not filed

frame record (number, index, transport_position, registration, error, done False until filed, exposure/gain/offset, rotation/flipped, prescan fields on walks) replaces an earlier record of that number; written whole via temp + fsync + retried rename (.bak on the run's first write); write failures kept in memory (unsaved) and retried. CLI: record_of.record at 781 and final save after writer.finish (814-830)
frames.close() ends the generator; _frame_rotation/_frame_flip cleared; on session close writer.finish, unsaved manifests saved once more, compact of uncompressed entries

flows.name: 4. Demo: DemoScanner inputs through the same path

steps.does: --demo: ScanSession(root=--library or demo/library, reference=demo/calibration/shading.npz, rolls=demo/rolls), settings demo/gui-settings.json; session._open_scanner = DemoScanner(--demo-source (real library, read), entry, no_film=--look-only, libraries_beside, cache=demo/pictures.npz). Window, ScanSession, FrameWriter and library.save are the real ones; the GUI stores self.demo and uses look_only only for dialog text
lists source entries; picture signatures cached on a daemon thread; best_pair
sleeps 210/speed s (1/speed s for reuse, whether or not a cache exists), sets _calibrated, returns no reference key; writes nothing

IR/film ValueError; DirectScanner.correctable_at/uncorrectable; DirectScanner.uncalibrated on the _calibrated flag; then _need_film (UsbError with --look-only); auto_exposure is DirectScanner.auto_exposure on demo probes; _work sleeps estimate_seconds/speed with progress. No suspect state, no command log, no debug spool

picks the strip entry at the roll position, or the entry for the film nearest 1800 dpi with raw bytes; library.decode_raw of the real raw bytes (upright, stagger replay) with the entry's shading.npz/ccd_mask; fallbacks: stored scan.tif (legacy corrected flagged), prescan.tif (corrected unless taken raw), synthetic test card

nearest-neighbour index maps to the shape recorded for that dpi; column roll by the simulated film position (_shift uses framing.APERTURE_MM/width); depth via _at_depth; a clear IR plane added when missing; reference resampled to the shown columns and the mask dropped when columns moved

pixels encoded as index lines in carriage order (bottom-up when the modelled carriage is far), decoded by the driver; last_raw/layout when keep_raw; capture set; apply_shading last, or raw with UNCALIBRATED_SOURCE where the real scan would refuse; meta demo=True, demo_source, read_direction, modelled carriage_state, DEVICE_SETTINGS exposure; no protocol_revision/commands/mode/filter_offsets/shading_origin
steps.data: bytes, upright raw, corrected image, meta

steps.does: identical to Flow 1 steps 13-18: fitted raw pixels, encoded bytes and pass reference filed into demo/library (or into --library if given); views and Save As via library.corrected

the driver's roll loop, hold and aim run on the stand-in; demo nudge moves _film_mm with DirectScanner.param_for_mm/STEP_MM/OVERHEAD_MM plus a retyped backlash (2.2 * 0.1057 mm); strips from _strip_for/_next_strip; one slipping frame per strip (index 2)

flows.name: 5. Offline: library entry -> corrected / reconstruct / verify / migrate / analysis

steps.does: globs */scan.json one level deep; adds _dir
tiff.read scan.tif + record + ShadingReference.load + mask bytes

'already' when corrections_applied has shading; 'deliberately raw' for SHADING_SKIPPED_EXPLICIT; 'raw -- correction was asked for'; 'no reference'; else apply_shading with today's code. Used by the GUI view (4593), Save As/Save all/Export (_deliver_one 4330), tools/make_comparison.py:136, dpi_analysis, linearity, registration_margin
raw.bin when no raw.bin.gz, else gunzip whole into memory; ScanParameters from the layout; decode_index; _replay (7200 dpi stagger)
decode_index; legacy corrected entries re-shaded (before _replay); _replay; compares shape, recorded direction, exact equality, legacy bottom-up; exit 1 when any decode changed

INCOMPLETE / missing or unreadable scan.json dirs; id vs dir; scan.tif sha; reference/mask presence; files{} sha; missing reference (except explicit raw, demo, uncalibrated-on-purpose tag); raw presence and sha of the decompressed bytes. Calibration archives are not checked

reconstruct + decode_raw; mislabelled entries only if one shading explains them, labelled entries unconditionally; rewrite scan.tif to the plain decode (old kept as scan.before-migrate-raw.tif), update image fields, reindex
records read_direction from raw tags, turns bottom-up scan.tif, judges prescan.tif by correlation (REVERSAL_MARGIN) and turns it when decisive
rmtree only entries whose raw sha (else image sha) equals a kept entry of the same signature
'Keep the library entry?' No -> shutil.rmtree(entry) + reindex, only for entries inside session.root
raw.bin -> raw.bin.gz verified against sha, TIFFs rewritten compressed, record updated; called only from ScanSession._run's finally
own decode through DirectScanner._deinterleave (no stagger replay) plus the entry reference

reuse and exists -> load_shading (713); else calibrate, archive (749) to <cache dir>/<UTC>/ and cache via save_shading (736, .shading.part.npz + os.replace). Paths are CWD-relative (GUI home/calibration/shading.npz; tools --reference)
window reads the cache's existence and mtime for 'reuse' and the prompt's age note; CLI --reuse shows no age
every corrected pass records shading_origin (calibrated: resolution, width, measured_utc, archive path; loaded: path, mtimes) in the entry's extra

gui-settings.json sections controls/film/output/window/presets/shortcuts/rolls/sheet; unreadable file moved aside (.unreadable-<time>); written whole via .part + replace (no fsync, json without default=str: a non-JSON value makes save return None, which is logged)
calibrate_shading() without keep_data and reference.save(reference_path) written in place (no archive, not atomic)

module_dependencies.notes: Leaf: SCSI constants, units, Settings, exceptions.

Cycle direct <-> library broken only by the lazy import. The offline decode (decode_index, _realign_native_column_stagger) lives on the USB driver class, so every offline reader imports the driver module.
Orchestration also owns delivery (export/preview) and roll manifests.

Not a subclass; borrows DirectScanner.scan_roll/_hold_to_approved/_aim_frame/_rejudge_for/auto_exposure/param_for_mm/roll_ends/place_on_strip and transport constants as class attributes (demo.py:787-813). DEVICE_SETTINGS and the backlash distance are its own.
Hands tools.frame_edges.walk_reader to the session as edge_reader. Recomputes APERTURE_MM (gui.py:213) with the same formula as framing.APERTURE_MM (framing.py:373) instead of importing it.
Drives the scanner itself (calibrate_shading/scan) outside ScanSession.

module_dependencies.module: tools probes (byte14_probe, gain_probe, fast_ir_probe, exposure_probe, hold_probe, transport_probe, transport_truth, roll_registration_walk, verify_protocol, filing_load_test, check_scanner)
module_dependencies.notes: Bypass paths; session_start() is called only here.

persisted_state.what: Scanner raw bytes of one pass
persisted_state.format: gzip level 6 (or plain) of INDEX lines: 2-byte tag + bytes_per_line, in the order received (bottom-up passes not reversed)
persisted_state.written_by: library.save (library.py:274-300) from capture_record or the debug raw_path; library.compact (414)
persisted_state.read_by: read_raw (604) -> decode_raw, reconstruct, verify, demo._decode, migrate_direction; tools/uniformity.py, tools/exposure_headroom.py
persisted_state.exact: byte-exact with sha256 of the uncompressed bytes; a payload followed by CHECK CONDITION never reaches it (F17); lines after an early EndOfData are simply absent

persisted_state.format: TIFF uint16 (uint8 for prescans) (H,W,C) RGB[I]; deflate with tifffile when compress, uncompressed for window single passes until compact
persisted_state.raw_or_corrected: raw decode, upright, 7200 dpi stagger-trimmed; corrected only when image.corrections_applied=['shading'] (FrameWriter fallback, legacy)

persisted_state.what: Shading reference used for the pass
persisted_state.format: np.savez_compressed: ref{c}/dark{c} float64[pixels_per_line], mean{c}/darkmean{c} float64, channels, dark_channels, pixels_per_line; compressed even when compress=False
persisted_state.raw_or_corrected: derived reduction of calibration bytes that are not in the entry
persisted_state.read_by: load, corrected, reconstruct (legacy), demo._decode, tools/library.py _one_shading_explains, exposure_headroom
persisted_state.exact: exact float64; the data.bin it came from is outside the entry and is linked only on a fresh calibration

persisted_state.format: raw bytes, length = reference pixels_per_line (0x00 used / 0x70 unused)
persisted_state.exact: yes; absent for demo passes whose columns were resampled

persisted_state.what: Framing prescan stored with a roll frame
persisted_state.raw_or_corrected: CORRECTED (raw when the roll ran shading=False), not labelled in the record
persisted_state.written_by: library.save:270 from session._file prescan=rf.prescan and tools/scan_roll.py (writer.submit prescan=frame.prescan)
persisted_state.exact: lossless TIFF of corrected pixels; its raw pixels, bytes and own mask are not stored (F03)

persisted_state.format: JSON indent=2, default=str; written via .part + fsync + one os.replace
persisted_state.raw_or_corrected: metadata: image, raw (layout), scan (SCAN_FIELDS), extra (commands, mode, started_utc, shading_origin, roll_membership, bracket_*, demo...), device, device_settings, metering, registration, calibration (report, skipped, light_mean rounded 0.1), prescan, film, tags, provenance, files (sha256)
persisted_state.read_by: entries, load, verify, reconstruct, demo, gui roll_entry_index/roll_summary, analysis tools
persisted_state.exact: yes except values JSON cannot carry (stringified), metering levels rounded to 4 dp, roll/bracket frames without metering (F04), hold/aim verification prescans and metering probes recording film='negative' (F31)

persisted_state.written_by: reindex (library.py:1045) after every save/tag/delete/migrate, non-atomic write_text

persisted_state.path_pattern: calibration/shading.npz (CWD-relative; demo/calibration/... under --demo, never written by the demo)

persisted_state.format: raw bytes / npz (compressed) / JSON (commands, sha256, geometry, protocol_revision)
persisted_state.written_by: archive_calibration (direct.py:749) inside ensure_shading, device open, plain writes (npz compressed)
persisted_state.read_by: nothing in rps7200/ or tools/; linked from entries only via extra.shading_origin.archive on a fresh calibration
persisted_state.exact: yes; not verified, not in the library
yes; claimed passes also spooled and kept until close (F08); never flushed after force abort or a failing t.close() (F12)

persisted_state.format: JSON via write_manifest (temp + fsync + retried rename)
persisted_state.raw_or_corrected: metadata: settings, frames[number, index, transport_position, registration marks, prescan file, prescan_rotation/flipped]
persisted_state.read_by: ScanSession._roll (carry), gui read_survey/roll_summary, scan_roll hold_from_walk (plain json.loads)
persisted_state.exact: yes; only home of walk registration/aim evidence (F14)

persisted_state.raw_or_corrected: metadata: settings, wanted, frames[registration, exposure/gain/offset, done, entry, filing_error, rotation/flipped]
persisted_state.written_by: RollManifest.record/filed (scanner and writer threads, locked); CLI final save

persisted_state.raw_or_corrected: corrected; window oriented by the session pair, CLI as scanned
persisted_state.written_by: FrameWriter export.write (window) / tiff.write on the scanning thread with the device open (scan_roll.py:660, 693)
persisted_state.exact: lossless of corrected pixels; -before files are in no library entry

persisted_state.format: TIFF uint16, oriented and optionally mono (window); unoriented and never mono (CLI)
persisted_state.exact: not re-derivable byte-identically later; overwritten on rescan (no _unclaimed)

persisted_state.format: JSON: frames[number, offset_mm (4 dp), rotation, flipped, reference_entry, source, as_walked]
persisted_state.exact: offset rounded to 4 dp vs the full-precision value the hold used

persisted_state.written_by: FrameWriter export.write (name chosen by _unclaimed on the scanner thread)

persisted_state.exact: merged image exists only here; silently overwritten

persisted_state.what: Save As / Save all / Export files
persisted_state.raw_or_corrected: corrected via library.corrected, oriented; mono by the window's current setting

findings.title: A failed library.save loses the whole picture: delivered copies, raw capture and later bracket passes
findings.evidence: FrameWriter._write calls `entry = library.save(` before `for path in job.get("paths") or ():`; an exception leaves _write and _run only does `self.errors.append(...)`. tools/scan.py `for held in pending: entries.append(library.save(...))` is unguarded and export.write(out) comes after it. library.save ends `(path / INCOMPLETE).unlink(missing_ok=True)` then `reindex(root)`.
findings.description: The library is a single point of failure: when the save raises, the job's raw bytes, raw pixels and corrected image are dropped and no delivered copy is attempted. tools/scan.py loses every pass after the first failing one and the --out file. A reindex error after a complete save is reported as a failed filing.
findings.failure_scenario: Library disk nearly full, out_dir on another drive: library.save raises ENOSPC on frame 12 of a window roll; frame 12 is lost entirely and the roll stops. A --bracket 9 run whose pass 2 fails to save loses passes 2-9 and the merge.
findings.recommendation: Catch the library failure per job, still write the delivered copies, and spool the capture to a recovery folder; guard each save in tools/scan.py; log a reindex failure after a complete entry.

findings.title: tools/scan.py does not honour the first Ctrl-C outside a bracket; the second abandons the read
findings.evidence: console.py _handler: first Ctrl-C sets `self._requested = True` and prints 'stopping after the pass in flight'. tools/scan.py checks it only in `if args.bracket and interrupt.requested():`; the single-pass path goes ensure_shading -> s.scan(... auto_exposure ...) without checking it.
findings.description: A Ctrl-C during calibration or metering is announced as a stop but the tool runs the metering probes and the full pass anyway, inviting the second Ctrl-C that raises KeyboardInterrupt inside a read.
findings.failure_scenario: Ctrl-C during the 3-4 min calibration of a 3600 dpi RGBI auto-exposure run; the tool then runs probes and a ~200 s pass; the operator presses Ctrl-C again, read_planes is abandoned, the device is suspect and needs a power cycle.
findings.recommendation: Check interrupt.requested() after ensure_shading and between metering rounds; exit cleanly with 130.

findings.title: Roll frame entries store the corrected prescan as prescan.tif, unlabelled, without its raw pixels, bytes or CCD mask
findings.evidence: scan_roll keeps `raw_prescan = self.last_pixels_raw`; session._file passes `raw_image=rf.raw_image, prescan=rf.prescan, prescan_meta=rf.prescan_meta` and never rf.raw_prescan; library.save writes `tiff.write(str(path / "prescan.tif"), prescan, ...)` and records only file, read_direction, carriage_state.
findings.description: The prescan inside every roll-frame entry is flat-fielded by that day's code; its raw pixels are dropped and its own mask and bytes are never kept outside debug mode. The record does not say whether it is corrected (a shading=False roll stores it raw with the same record).
findings.failure_scenario: A later fix to apply_shading cannot reach any roll prescan; migrate_direction and the demo treat it as corrected even for shading=False rolls.
findings.recommendation: File rf.raw_prescan with its own mask and bytes (linked entry, or prescan_raw.tif + mask) and record the prescan's correction state.
findings.doc_reference: CLAUDE.md 'The library holds raw pixels; everything else is corrected.'

findings.title: Rolls and brackets drop the metering evidence and are recorded as exposure_metered False
findings.evidence: scan_roll: `scales = self.auto_exposure(...)` then `self.scan(..., exposure_scale=scales, ...)` without auto_exposure; scan() records `"exposure_metered": bool(auto_exposure)` and attaches metering only `if auto_exposure and self.last_metering is not None`. scan_bracket likewise.
findings.description: The two production multi-pass paths meter outside scan(), so every frame they file has metering null and claims a commanded exposure.
findings.failure_scenario: Every frame of a METER_EACH roll lacks the probe levels/targets that explain its exposure; blue clipping cannot be diagnosed from rolls.
findings.recommendation: Attach a copy of last_metering to each metered frame/pass and record which frame metered for METER_ONCE.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/direct.py auto_exposure docstring: ':meth:`scan` files it with the entry'

findings.title: Calibration bytes live outside the library and are unlinked when the reference is loaded from the cache
findings.evidence: `archive = self.archive_calibration(result, path.parent)`; the only link is `self._shading_origin["archive"] = str(archive)` on a fresh calibration; load_shading sets an origin with no archive. Nothing in rps7200/ or tools/ reads data.bin.
findings.description: Each entry keeps only the reduced shading.npz; the calibration bytes sit in a CWD-relative folder verify never checks, and reuse sessions do not name them.
findings.failure_scenario: After an improvement to calculate_shading, entries from --reuse sessions cannot be re-reduced; cleaning calibration/ loses every calibration's bytes silently.
findings.recommendation: Copy data.bin into each entry or carry the archive stamp/sha through the cache into shading_origin; teach verify to check it.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/library.py module docstring: entries are self-contained

findings.title: A suspect device is sent configuration writes before scan() refuses
findings.evidence: scan() has no _refuse_if_suspect; it sends READ STATE, TUR, set_exposure_time, set_highlight_shadow, set_scan_frame, cmd_17, get/set_gain_offset and set_mode before `self.slide(SLIDE_INIT, ...)`, which is the first call to `_refuse_if_suspect`. auto_exposure's set_gain_offset(base) likewise.
findings.description: After an abandoned pass about ten WRITE/MODE SELECT/vendor commands still reach the device before DeviceSuspect.
findings.failure_scenario: A pass times out; the operator presses Scan again; gain/offset, exposure, frame, cmd 0x17 and MODE SELECT go to a device possibly still streaming.
findings.recommendation: Call _refuse_if_suspect at the top of scan(), auto_exposure(), prescan() and scan_roll().
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/direct.py:522-524 'Set, it makes every command that would drive the device raise DeviceSuspect'

findings.title: tools/scan_roll.py keeps scanning after the library stops accepting frames
findings.evidence: `writer = FrameWriter()` has no on_done; failures reach only `record_of.filed(n, entry, error, ...)`. The window's _filed calls `self.request_stop()` on a filing error.
findings.description: CLI and window diverge: the CLI scans the rest of the strip into a failing library.
findings.failure_scenario: Library disk fills at frame 10 of 38; frames 10-38 are scanned and lost, about an hour of scanner time.
findings.recommendation: Give the tool's FrameWriter an on_done that sets the stop flag the roll already polls.

findings.title: The debug spool keeps every pass, claimed or not, on the temp disk until close()
findings.evidence: _debug_capture np.save's the raw pixels and writes raw.bin for every pass; debug_claim only sets `item["claimed"] = True`; unlinking happens only in _debug_flush from close().
findings.description: Claimed passes (already filed by their caller) still occupy temp disk for the whole session.
findings.failure_scenario: RPS7200_DEBUG=1 on a 38-frame 3600 dpi RGBI roll spools ~20 GB beside the library writes; on one disk library.save then fails (F01).
findings.recommendation: Unlink a claimed item's spool files in debug_claim.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/direct.py:1076-1085 'the peak is what runs a machine out of space'

findings.title: Library atomic renames have no retry for a file Windows holds briefly
findings.evidence: _write_atomic ends with one `os.replace(temp, path)`; the retries (REPLACE_RETRY_S, session._replace) exist only for manifests, whose comment explains Defender/indexer hold new files.
findings.description: scan.json, compacted TIFFs and the calibration cache are renamed without the retry the manifests need for the same reason.
findings.failure_scenario: On Windows Defender opens .scan.json.part; os.replace raises PermissionError; the entry stays INCOMPLETE, the frame is reported unfiled and the window stops the roll.
findings.recommendation: Route every library rename through one retrying replace.

findings.title: migrate-raw rewrites labelled entries without checking that the decode reproduces them
findings.evidence: `if np.array_equal(plain, stored) and not applied: continue`; `if not applied and not _one_shading_explains(...)`: failed; otherwise `planned.append(...)`; reconstruct's verdict is discarded for corrections_applied=['shading'].
findings.description: Labelled legacy entries are rewritten from today's decode whatever reconstruct said.
findings.failure_scenario: After a decode regression, migrate-raw --write launders the wrong decode into labelled entries; reconstruct then reports them identical.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite a labelled entry only when reconstruct's verdict is 'identical'.

findings.title: The CLI tools calibrate without asking whether the film is loaded
findings.evidence: tools/scan.py calls s.ensure_shading unconditionally; scan_roll.calibrate() likewise after the seek; the window refuses with 'Nothing started. Tick that the film is in the transport first'.
findings.description: The empty-transport calibration hazard is guarded only in the window.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator runs tools/scan.py with an empty transport; a measuring calibration runs in a state the vendor never creates and which preceded a wedge.
findings.recommendation: Require an explicit --film-loaded confirmation (or prompt) before a measuring calibration in the tools.
findings.doc_reference: CLAUDE.md 'Only Stefan can see the transport. Ask him.'

findings.title: Force abort skips close(), so debug-spooled passes are never filed and their location is never reported
findings.evidence: `if not self.dead: self._scanner.close()`; close() is the only caller of _debug_flush(); force_abort sets dead and closes only the transport. close() also skips the flush when t.close() raises.
findings.description: After a force abort (or a failing transport close) probes, hold/aim prescans and unclaimed passes remain in $TMP with no log line naming the directory.
findings.failure_scenario: A wedged pass is force-aborted; the metering probes that explain it are left in an unnamed temp directory.
findings.recommendation: Flush (or at least log the spool directory) after force abort, and call _debug_flush in a finally in close().

findings.title: Rolls have no up-front refusal of an uncorrectable resolution (window, demo and driver)
findings.evidence: The window accepts `self._int(self.v_dpi, "Scan dpi", 25, 7200)`; on_roll and on_scan_chosen never call correctable_at; scan_roll checks meter, film and IR only; auto_exposure runs before scan() raises uncorrectable. tools/scan_roll.py:332 does refuse.
findings.description: Each frame is prescanned, held and metered before scan() refuses it; the roll counts failures and moves film.
findings.failure_scenario: A 7200 dpi roll from the sheet: three frames are prescanned, nudged and metered, each refused, then the roll gives up.
findings.recommendation: Refuse in on_roll/on_scan_chosen and at the top of scan_roll when correctable_at is false and shading is on.

findings.title: Walk evidence exists only in the roll folder, which the Delete dialog calls re-derivable
findings.evidence: Walk prescans are filed with `dict(rf.prescan_meta or {...}, roll_membership=...)`, which has no registration; marks go only into survey.json; prescanNN-before.tif is written with `file_entry=False`. The dialog: 'The library entries are NOT touched: the raw bytes stay, and the frames can be rebuilt from them'.
findings.description: Deleting a walked roll folder destroys aim decisions, confidences and pre-aim pictures that exist nowhere else.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator deletes an old walk folder trusting the dialog; the registration history CONFIDENCE_FLOOR is fitted from is gone.
findings.recommendation: File walk registration into the prescan entries and file the -before prescan, or name these files in the dialog.
findings.doc_reference: tools/gui.py:2813-2815 'Everything in a roll folder is re-derivable from the library except approved.json'

findings.title: apply_shading leaves columns beyond the mask's used count uncorrected, and only logs it
findings.evidence: `return locs[:width]` and the loop writes only `out[:, : loc.size, c] = vals`; scan() refuses only `params.width > self._shading.pixels_per_line`.
findings.description: Corrected deliverables can carry unflat-fielded edge columns with nothing in the file saying so (report.columns < width only).
findings.failure_scenario: At 600 dpi the mask marks 860 used pixels against 862 columns; the last columns ship raw.
findings.recommendation: Warn or fill the uncovered columns, and surface report.columns < width in the record.

findings.title: The command log lists every NoDataYet poll; index.json is rebuilt from all entries on every save and read by nothing
findings.evidence: _CommandLog.command: `except Exception as exc: entry["refused"] = type(exc).__name__; self.record.append(entry)`; read_planes re-polls every 0.02 s on NoDataYet; reindex json-loads every entry; nothing reads index.json.
findings.description: Refused image READs are listed despite the 'counted, not listed' claim, bloating scan.json; every save re-parses the library.
findings.failure_scenario: A pass idle for 60 s adds ~3000 command entries to its scan.json.
findings.recommendation: Count NoDataYet polls in bulk; make reindex incremental or drop it.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/direct.py:441-443 'Image-data READs are counted, not listed'

findings.title: A payload followed by CHECK CONDITION is thrown away
findings.evidence: `payload = self._read_payload(read_size, timeout_ms)` then `if final == UsbStatus.CHECK: raise CheckCondition(command[0])`; read_lines(retries=1) turns that into EndOfData and read_planes does `except EndOfData: ... break`.
findings.description: If the device signals end-of-data as a CHECK after the last data-in, those bytes never reach last_raw or the decode, and the short pass is accepted without error.
findings.failure_scenario: A pass's last batch is dropped; the entry is filed short with no suspect and no record of the lost lines.
findings.recommendation: Return the payload with the condition (or keep it) and record lines_expected vs lines_received as a problem.

findings.title: A tools/scan.py bracket holds every pass several times in RAM until close
findings.evidence: pending holds raw pixels and capture['raw'] bytes of each pass, and scan_bracket runs with retain=True so `frames.append(image)` keeps every corrected pass.
findings.description: Passes are neither spooled nor written until the device closes.
findings.failure_scenario: A 9-pass 3600 dpi bracket holds several GB; an out-of-memory kill loses every pass.
findings.recommendation: Spool each pass to disk as it lands, as debug filing does.
findings.doc_reference: CLAUDE.md 'Each is spooled to a temporary file as it is taken'

findings.title: INFRARED_FLOOR_S guards nothing
findings.evidence: The only references are the definition and `INFRARED_FLOOR_S = DirectScanner.INFRARED_FLOOR_S`; read_idle_s uses READ_IDLE_S and UNTIED_INFRARED_IDLE_S.
findings.description: The comment says it sits 'beside the read it guards'; no read uses it.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader trusts the comment when tuning timeouts.
findings.recommendation: Remove it or use it; fix the comment.

findings.title: The demo retypes device constants and diverges in small behaviours
findings.evidence: `swallowed = min(abs(asked), 2.2 * 0.1057)`; `self._work(7.0)` per advance; `self._work(210.0 if not reuse else 1.0)`; ensure_shading answers 'loaded' for reuse=True with no cache (the real one measures); DEVICE_SETTINGS = Settings(exposure=[9604, 6506, 6506, 7745], ...) retyped; demo metas carry no protocol_revision, commands, mode, filter_offsets or shading_origin.
findings.description: Retyped constants and behaviours the rule forbids.
findings.failure_scenario: The real reuse-without-cache path (a 3-4 minute measurement) is shown as a 1 s load in the demo.
findings.recommendation: Take these from DirectScanner/session constants and mirror ensure_shading's reuse fallback.

findings.title: The demo files uncorrected passes where the driver refuses, and verify has an if-demo branch
findings.evidence: _take: `elif reference is not None: image, report = apply_shading(...)` else `skipped = UNCALIBRATED_SOURCE`; DirectScanner.scan raises ShadingUnavailable there. verify: `demo = bool((record.get("extra") or {}).get("demo"))` suppresses the missing-reference problem.
findings.description: A shading=True demo pass from an entry without a reference is shown and filed raw, a path the scanner never takes.
findings.failure_scenario: The demo files and shows striped raw frames the real scanner would refuse.
findings.recommendation: Raise as the driver does, or choose another source entry.

findings.title: Analysis tools decode without the stagger replay; the uniformity study calibrates without archiving
findings.evidence: Both call `DirectScanner._deinterleave(raw, params, ...)` instead of library.decode_raw; uniformity calls `scanner.calibrate_shading()` (keep_data False) and `reference.save(reference_path)` in place.
findings.description: Two decode paths for stored bytes, and a calibration path that keeps no bytes.
findings.failure_scenario: A 7200 dpi entry analysed by these tools is 4 rows off from scan.tif.
findings.recommendation: Use library.decode_raw and ensure_shading/archive_calibration.

findings.title: Silent overwrites in the CLI tools
findings.evidence: --out defaults to 'scan.tif' and `out.with_suffix(".json").write_text(...)` follows; scan_roll writes `out / f"frame{number:02d}.tif"` and prescanNN.tif without _unclaimed and replaces survey.json on each --dry-run.
findings.description: Repeated runs overwrite delivered files and walks without warning.
findings.failure_scenario: Two tools/scan.py runs in one folder: the first scan.tif and its sidecar are gone.
findings.recommendation: Use _unclaimed or refuse to overwrite without --force.

findings.title: In the window's Delete, the destructive answer is 'No'
findings.evidence: `keep = messagebox.askyesnocancel("Delete", question + "\n\nKeep the library entry?")` ... `if not keep: shutil.rmtree(entry)`
findings.description: Answering No to a 'Keep?' question removes raw bytes irreversibly.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator clicks No meaning 'do not delete' and loses the entry.
findings.recommendation: Ask 'Delete the library entry too?' with the destructive answer as an explicit button.

findings.title: Stale transport and unit statements in code and docs
findings.evidence: plan_nudges docstring: 'an integer param in 1..8' and 'param_for_mm already clamps silently at param 8' while MAX_CORRECTION_PARAM = 87; scan_roll prints 'offset the film by ... mm' and 'SHORT BY ... mm'.
findings.description: Comments describe a cap and a ramp that have changed; the CLI speaks millimetres to the operator.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer sizes a correction from the stale cap.
findings.recommendation: Update the comments and print units.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/protocol.py:227 'Millimetres are prohibited in anything an operator reads'

findings.title: Entries left uncompressed by a killed window have no CLI command to compact them
findings.evidence: The action choices are list/verify/reconstruct/reindex/duplicates/migrate-raw/migrate-direction/tag; library.compact is called only from ScanSession._run's finally.
findings.description: Plain raw.bin and uncompressed TIFFs stay double size forever.
findings.failure_scenario: A window killed during a session leaves its entries uncompressed permanently.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'compact' action.

findings.title: Save As, Save all and Export write TIFFs without a resolution tag
findings.evidence: _deliver_one: `note = export.write(path, full, quality=quality)`; FrameWriter: `export.write(str(path), delivered, resolution=job["dpi"], ...)`.
findings.description: The same picture carries a DPI when written by a roll and none when exported.
findings.failure_scenario: An exported frame opens at 72 dpi in an editor.
findings.recommendation: Pass the entry's resolution_dpi.

findings.title: Debug entries ignore the caller's library root and film notes
findings.evidence: `root = os.environ.get(self.DEBUG_ROOT_ENV) or library.DEFAULT_ROOT`; `film=FilmNotes(notes="captured with RPS7200_DEBUG on")`; the spooled meta is copied before scan_roll adds roll_index and registration.
findings.description: Probes and hold prescans are filed apart from the roll and library they belong to (e.g. ./library while the window files into demo/library or --library).
findings.failure_scenario: A demo-less window run with --library elsewhere: its probes land in ./library.
findings.recommendation: Let the session pass its root and film notes to the scanner.

findings.title: session_start's opening SLIDE is the sub-frame forward action and runs only in probes
findings.evidence: `self.slide(0x00, param=0x01)` sends `00 01 00 00`, while nudge sends `0x00 <param> 00 04`; session_start() is called only by probe tools.
findings.description: Probe sessions open with a command the production paths never send.
findings.failure_scenario: A probe's findings differ from production because of a param-1 forward move at open.
findings.recommendation: Document or remove.

findings.title: A calibration ends on any refused read and builds (or discards) the reference from whatever arrived
findings.evidence: calibrate_shading loop: `chunk = self.read_lines(4, bpl, retries=1)` ... `except (EndOfData, ScanReadError): self._log(f"  scanner finished after {blocks} blocks"); ended = True; break`. read_lines raises ScanReadError for any non-end-of-data sense ('was refused'). Then `self._shading = calculate_shading(data, width)` with no check of blocks against the descriptor's declared lines; calculate_shading treats all lines as light when max/min level < 5. session._calibrate comment: 'A calibration that failed part way leaves the reference the session already had' -- only in its except branch.
findings.description: Any refused calibration read (a one-shot condition, the ASC 0x20 refusal the code notes a disturbed calibration produces) is taken as the scanner finishing. With few or only unlit lines the reference is built silently from them (single-point from dark lines if the phases do not split), and every corrected pass and deliverable of the session uses it. With zero lines calculate_shading returns None and the session's previous good in-memory reference is overwritten with None; _shading_origin still says 'calibrated'.
findings.failure_scenario: A calibration is refused after 3 blocks (only dark lines arrived): the reference is the dark floor, ensure_shading reports success and caches it over calibration/shading.npz, and every corrected scan and Save As of the session is badly wrong until someone looks. Raw entries survive, but the cache is poisoned for later 'reuse' sessions.
findings.recommendation: Treat only EndOfData as the end; compare lines received per channel against get_shading_parms' declared lines and require both phases (or a plausible light level) before replacing _shading or the cache.
findings.doc_reference: rps7200/session.py:2048-2049 'A calibration that failed part way leaves the reference the session already had'

findings.title: Hold/aim verification prescans and metering probes record film='negative' whatever the film
findings.evidence: _hold_to_approved: `image, _ = self.prescan(resolution=prescan_resolution, keep_raw=keep_raw, shading=shading)` (no film); auto_exposure probe: `self.scan(resolution=resolution, infrared=False, exposure_scale=scales, shading=shading, keep_raw=True)` (no film). scan_roll then takes `prescan_meta = dict(self.last_scan_meta or {})` from the verification pass, and a walk files `dict(rf.prescan_meta ..., roll_membership=...)` as the entry meta.
findings.description: A walk with the automatic nudge on files each moved frame's prescan with scan.film='negative' for slide or B&W film, and debug-filed probes and hold prescans are always 'negative'. library.signature, demo._source_for and _pool_for select by scan.film.
findings.failure_scenario: A B&W walk with 'correct' ticked: every corrected frame's prescan entry says negative, the demo later serves it for colour negative, and a search by film misses it.
findings.recommendation: Pass film through _hold_to_approved/_aim_frame to prescan() and through auto_exposure to its probes.

findings.title: On a real roll, prescans of failed frames and of the blank frame that ends the roll are never filed
findings.evidence: session._roll files rf.prescan only `if job.dry_run:`; for a real roll it rides with the frame (`prescan=rf.prescan` in the rf.image branch), and `if rf.error: self._emit("log", ...)` files nothing. scan_roll yields `RollFrame(index, position, None, {}, prescan_image, marks, error=str(exc), raw_prescan=raw_prescan, ...)`; the blank-contrast branch `return`s without yielding. tools/scan_roll.py: `if frame.error: failed += 1` only.
findings.description: The prescan, its raw pixels and bytes of exactly the frames that went wrong reach the library only when RPS7200_DEBUG is on; otherwise they are dropped, contradicting 'file every scan'.
findings.failure_scenario: Frame 17 fails with a ScanReadError after its prescan and hold; the evidence of where the film sat and what the frame looked like exists only in roll.json's registration numbers.
findings.recommendation: File rf.prescan with rf.raw_prescan (kind='prescan') whenever the frame did not produce an entry, and file the blank prescan before ending the roll.

findings.title: tools/scan_roll.py delivers frames unoriented and never monochrome, unlike the window's roll
findings.evidence: CLI writer.submit(number, paths, dpi, image, raw_image, meta, prescan, prescan_meta, library, inquiry, capture, tags, film, on_filed) has no mono/mono_channel/rotate/flip keys, so FrameWriter's `job.get("mono")` is None; the window passes `mono=wants_mono(job.mono, job.film)` and an orientation. scan_roll has no --mono option.
findings.description: The same roll of B&W film scanned from the CLI yields 3-channel frameNN.tif, from the window 1-channel; consumers that rely on the shape to recognise B&W (rps7200/mono.py's rationale) get it wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: A B&W roll scanned with tools/scan_roll.py is inverted by NegPy as colour.
findings.recommendation: Add --mono/--no-mono (default by film) and pass mono to the writer, as tools/scan.py does.

findings.title: The CLI walk compresses TIFFs on the scanning thread with the device open
findings.evidence: `tiff.write(str(pre), frame.prescan)` and `tiff.write(str(was), frame.prescan_before)` (compress defaults to True) run in the generator loop between passes. session.py: 'Written by the writer thread, not here: ... nothing local happens on the scanning thread with the device open.'
findings.description: The CLI does on the scanning thread what the window deliberately moved to the writer thread; small, but it is the open-and-idle compression the project avoids.
findings.failure_scenario: On a slow disk each walked frame leaves the device idle while deflate runs, the state that preceded a wedge.
findings.recommendation: Submit these files through the FrameWriter as the window does.

findings.title: Save As, Save all and Export use the window's current mono setting, not the pass's film
findings.evidence: `self._deliver_one(result, path, jpeg_quality(...), self.v_mono.get(), self.v_mono_channel.get())`; Export: `mono, channel = self.v_mono.get(), self.v_mono_channel.get()`; _deliver_one: `if mono: full = to_monochrome(full, mono_channel)`.
findings.description: A colour roll exported while the film selector says B&W comes out monochrome, and a B&W roll exported with colour selected comes out RGB, differing from its own frameNN.tif.
findings.failure_scenario: After scanning a B&W strip the operator switches the film to negative for the next strip, then exports the B&W roll: all frames are 3-channel.
findings.recommendation: Decide mono from the entry's scan.film (wants_mono) rather than the live control.

findings.title: --demo with --library files demo passes into a real library
findings.evidence: `root=args.library or str(home / "library")` where home is demo/ only for the default.
findings.description: `gui.py --demo --library library` writes resampled demo passes (with fitted, not scanned, bytes) into the real library, where they share signatures with real entries; only extra.demo distinguishes them and verify then hides their missing references.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator adds --library to point the demo at pictures (the flag is --demo-source) and pollutes library/ with synthetic entries.
findings.recommendation: Refuse --library pointing at the demo source or at the default real library under --demo.

findings.title: UNTIED_INFRARED_IDLE_S comment describes a different sum than the value
findings.evidence: Comment: 'What an untied infrared pass may sit silent for: the floor plus the 227 s top of its measured range, and a minute on top.' Code: `UNTIED_INFRARED_IDLE_S = 227.0 + 60.0`.
findings.description: The floor (212 s) is not added; the value is 287 s, matching CLAUDE.md, but the comment implies 499 s.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer 'fixes' the value to match the comment.
findings.recommendation: Reword the comment.

findings.title: 'Uncompressed' writes with the device open still compress the shading reference
findings.evidence: archive_calibration: 'Written uncompressed: the device is still open'; library.save: '``compress=False`` writes the raw bytes as `raw.bin` and the TIFFs uncompressed: plain writes'; both call ShadingReference.save, which is `np.savez_compressed(path, **arrays)`.
findings.description: Every window single scan and every calibration archive deflates a few hundred kB with the device open and idle, contrary to the stated rule; small, but the docstrings say it does not happen.
findings.failure_scenario: Low risk; misleads anyone auditing what runs with the device open.
findings.recommendation: Add a compress flag to ShadingReference.save or correct the docstrings.

findings.title: The window accepts zero or negative exposure factors and the device silently gets the 100-count floor
findings.evidence: _exposure returns any parsed numbers; Settings.scaled: `int(max(100, min(65535, round(e * f))))`.
findings.description: Typing 0 or a negative factor is not refused; the pass runs at exposure 100 (nearly black) and is filed with exposure_scale 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A mistyped '0.8' as '0,8' parses as two factors 0 and 8: red at the floor, green at 8x, a wasted pass.
findings.recommendation: Validate 0 < factor and the per-channel count in _exposure.

findings.title: Debug filing never runs under --demo
findings.evidence: DemoScanner has no debug, _debug_capture, _debug_flush or debug_claim; session._file uses `getattr(self._scanner, "debug_claim", None)`.
findings.description: The claim/flush path that files metering probes and hold/aim prescans is below the seam in DirectScanner, so the demo cannot exercise it.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression in debug_claim or _debug_flush is invisible in make run-demo.
findings.recommendation: Note it as untested with no device, or move the spool into a mixin the stand-in also uses.
